newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin, feeling "absolutely normal", sees Chubais.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin, feeling "absolutely normal", sees Chubais.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin, said to be feeling "absolutely normal" after heart surgery, met his Kremlin chief of staff on Friday and was also due to hold talks with Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin.

Interfax news agency said Yeltsin received Anatoly Chubais, head of the Kremlin administration, at the Barvikha sanatorium outside Moscow where he is recovering after his multple bypass operation on November 5.
The agency said they had discussed a wide range of issues, including delays in payment of wages and pensions, and planned army reforms.

They also discussed an extraordinary session being held by the opposition-dominated lower house of parliament on Yeltsin's decision to pull the last Russian troops out of breakaway Chechnya. Interfax gave no details.

Chernomyrdin was expected to see Yeltsin later on Friday. RIA news agency said he was likely to brief the president about his visits this week to France and Poland, and a European security summit which he is due to attend in Portugal next week.

Itar-Tass news agency quoted chief Kremlin doctor Sergei Mironov as saying Yeltsin was taking two or three walks a day and gradually building up his exercise load. He said the 65-year-old president was feeling "absolutely normal".

Mironov confirmed that Yeltsin would be able to start visiting the Kremlin from December 5, one month after the operation, and would be able to have a "fuller" work schedule from December 20. He gave no other details.
